findings.reason: the section must name its net public-definition delta in one unambigous figure, because that figure is the whole interface-budget rule and the two statements in its own text cannot both be true.
findings.text: the interface-accounting paragraph says the stripper conversion "keeps the family at 1481 and the section's net addition is one public definition", while the done-when says "public_definitions at the first node's head is exactly one higher than at its base and at the second node's head equal to its base"; read from the actual base these disagree (1480→1481→1481 is a net +1, not a return to base), and the section's "nothing is retired, because the identity digest and the prose walk keep their names" clause omits the interim public `strip_tags` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:1880`) it does retire to `_strip_tags`

findings.reason: both modules live in the `reckon.crew` package, which the plan's own house rule (a shared-package definition stays private) admits, so this is a consistency note the §22 author can record rather than a design change.
findings.text: §22 reads `dispatch._normalised_words` (a `_`-prefixed tokeniser) from `plan_review.py` while §16 elsewhere treats a cross-module private read as a defect it repairs (`_REVIEW_SIDECAR_NAME`)

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `section_prose` hides boundary discovery, skip-tag subtraction, entity decoding and whitespace normalisation behind one reader, and `_review_coverage` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:510`) already joins `list_plan_reviews` to `roadmap.implementable_sections` with no walk of its own.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §21's report-directory consolidation is correct (`delivered_reports` at `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:880` rebuilds the same `reports_dir()/project/"plan-review"/slug` root that `review_report_directory` builds at `:791`), but §22 introduces a second consumer of a module-private tokeniser across module boundaries — `dispatch._normalised_words` (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:289`) read from `reckon/crew/plan_review.py` — beside the plan's own rule that a shared tokeniser earns a shared name.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16's interface accounting and its done-when state the public_definitions delta inconsistently, so a reader cannot check the one rule the section exists to satisfy.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the section runs its own censuses and reuses the named machinery; the prose-reader census `grep -rn 'stripped_strings\|get_text(' reckon/` returns 14 lines and the three plan-prose readers (`reckon/mcp_views.py:2072` `authored_plan_text`, `reckon/mcp_views.py:2238` `_section_response`, `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:343` `_plan_section_text`) converge on `section_prose`; `_TAG_RE` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:1876`), `_PROSE_SKIP_TAGS` (`:1877`), `section_record_id` (`:90`), `structured_section_spans` (`:415`), `is_implementable_section` (`reckon/_schema.py:788`) and `review_report_directory` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:791`) are all cited and extended rather than rebuilt.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §23 justifies extending `routing._store_delivered_plan_review` (`reckon/crew/routing.py:2582`) into the single public `store_delivered_reviews` rather than adding a parallel store step, and §16 merges the span rule into one private function both projections call.
